title: Women musicians with bands
summary: She recalls little about women instrumentalists beyond a Baton Rouge woman and says it was hard for women to travel.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You mentioned Jeanette Kimball as another lady who worked with bands in the same area you lived in, and she was in New Orleans, but you said there were others that you couldn't think of any other names. Have you been able to think of the names of any other women who were professional musicians working with bands?

Not right in Lake Charles. Now, there was a -- dear me -- there was a girl in Baton Rouge, Louisiana that was very, very well known at the time, around that area. You know, they just didn't used to travel around very much, the women didn't, for some reason. They didn't, and of course I can understand that, because some of them were -- you know, they had families or had other careers, no doubt.
I imagine it was a little bit more difficult --
It was difficult, it really was, you know, it was awfully hard. It really was. It wasn't like it is today. It was hard, very hard.
